note: Every parameter of the flying-fish simulator, with its source. kind = measured (from a fetched source), secondary (quoted second-hand in a fetched source), assumed (no source; the value is a modelling choice and the slider range shows how much it matters), tuned (chosen so a sourced quantity is reproduced; which one is named). Nothing here comes from a bird. The second fish is HYPOTHETICAL: a design study that changes only morphology and physiology parameters (see physics/flier/spec.json); the equations are the real fish's.

rho_air.note: sea level; same value as physics/analysis.py

fish.label: Darkedged-wing flying fish, Park and Choi 2010 specimen L3

ref_area_m2.source: park-choi-2010 Table 1 model L3: A1 + A2 + A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform), the reference area of its coefficients

span_m.source: park-choi-2010 Table 1 model L3 (full pectoral span S)

CL_at_zero_deg.source: no value in the text (it is in Fig. 5, not read); chosen inside the plausible range; with LD_max it fixes the drag polar

CL_slope_per_deg.source: (CL_max - CL_at_zero_deg) / 35 deg, linear up to the stall at 35 deg; shape assumed

CD_k.source: CD = CD_min + k CL^2 with k fixed by CD(0 deg) = CL(0 deg) / LD_max; quadratic polar shape assumed

stall_alpha_deg.source: park-choi-2010: lift coefficient largest at 30-35 deg

glide_alpha_deg.source: the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface

body_frontal_area_m2.source: no body depth or width in the sources; 0.0007 m^2 is a 30 mm by 30 mm ellipse-sized section for a 203 mm fish

water_drag_coefficient.source: no measured value for a flying fish; frontal-area drag coefficient of a streamlined body

approach_speed_m_s.source: makiguchi-2013 Discussion citing Davenport 1994: approach and leap at approximately 10 m/s (20 to 30 body lengths per second)

swim_thrust_N.source: set equal to the water drag at the approach speed, so the submerged fish reaches 10 m/s (the secondary field value) and no faster

taxi_thrust_N.source: set to the swim thrust times a factor; default 0.7 after the run-6 sweep (0.15 to 0.7): below about 0.6 the assumed lobe water drag never lets the fish reach the speed at which the fins must lift it (about 16 m/s), so it taxis indefinitely; at 0.7 it taxis about 15 m, lifts off at 16.5 m/s and glides 36 m. The factor therefore compensates for two assumed hydrodynamic values (lobe drag area fraction, water drag coefficient) and is post-hoc. The lobe sculls at up to 50 beats per second (davenport-1994) but no thrust was measured; 2.5 N is about four body weights

lobe_length_m.source: length of the enlarged lower caudal lobe below the body axis; not in the sources; 0.05 m is a quarter of standard length

pitch_at_leap_deg.source: makiguchi-2013 Table 3: 20.0 +- 3.3 deg in captivity; field studies cited there give about 30 deg

start_depth_m.source: where the run starts; it only sets how long the swim phase lasts

reentry_min_speed_m_s.source: below this speed at re-entry the fish is taken to stop taxiing and submerge; not in the sources

max_glides.source: stops the run; field sequences of 400 m in 30 s (park-choi-2010 introduction) imply several taxi-glide cycles

ground_effect.source: park-choi-2010 Fig. 12 and text (physics/ground-effect.json): lift unchanged; drag times 1 for h/b >= 0.97, falling linearly to 0.86 at h/b = 0.33 over water, held at 0.86 below that (not measured lower)

approach_angle_deg.source: path angle of the swim toward the surface. Davenport 1994 (abstract): the fish leaps through the surface at a shallow angle; the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path. Added after run 2 (deviation, physics/sim/RUNS.md)

takeoff_speed_target_m_s.source: the speed at which the fish stops trimming low and lets itself lift off; Davenport 1994 says the fish accelerates to take-off speed by taxiing with the fins expanded; free-flight airspeed is 15 to 20 m/s (secondary), so 17.5 is the midpoint. Added after run 2 (deviation)

taxi_trim.source: behaviour: during the taxi the fish sets its angle of attack each step so lift balances weight at a target height of half the lobe length, with a damping term on vertical speed (gains 2 per m and 2 s per m, assumed; added after the run-5 sweep showed the undamped trim let the body creep out of the water at 10 m/s), bounded between -10 deg and the stall; the tail stays in the water until even -10 deg gives more lift than weight (about 16 m/s with this polar) or the take-off speed target; then it holds the glide angle of attack. Replaces the fixed taxi pitch of run 2 (deviation; post-hoc)

breach_model.value: vertical velocity set to zero at the surface, on exit and on re-entry
breach_model.source: Davenport 1994 (abstract): the fish leaps through the surface at a shallow angle and then taxis with the tail beating. The model has no planing support from the water, so the shallow exit is represented by zeroing the vertical velocity when the body centre crosses z = -lobe; without it the 10 deg approach carries 1.7 m/s of upward momentum through the 5 cm taxi band and the fish pops out in half a metre (runs 2 and 3). Added after run 3 (deviation; tests 1-3 are post-hoc from run 2 on) The same rule applies on re-entry (the fish lowers the tail into the water and keeps the body out: Deng 2019 introduction), added after run 4.

powered.source: davenport-1994 abstract point 6: flying fish do not flap their wings to gain lift; the real fish gets no flapping thrust in the model. Test 4 (whether its muscles COULD power flight) waits for the physiology chain

flight_muscle_fraction.source: not reported for any flying fish; Davenport 1992 (abstract): no more red axial muscle than a cruising mackerel

fish.label: HYPOTHETICAL designed flier F1 (design study, physics/flier/spec.json): same 60 g body, fins at bat-like wing loading, flight muscle 16 % of body mass

ref_area_m2.source: design choice: wing loading 12 N/m2 (inside the bat range 6.5-14.25 N/m2 in comparison-data.csv; below pterosaur hatchlings 15.8-17.9, PMC8298463); 3.9x the real reference area

span_m.source: from the lifting area at the fish's own aspect ratio 9 (Park and Choi 9.0-10.7); 2.5x the real span

powered.source: the design question: flapping thrust from the flight muscle once airborne

flight_muscle_fraction.source: smallest fraction that covers a 1 m/s climb at the bat-derived maximum specific power; bats: mean 9.13 %, minimum 7.8 % (PMC10966098 citing Bullen and McKenzie 2004); the bat maximum was not found

muscle_specific_power_W_per_kg.source: Pipistrellus nathusii maximum mechanical flight power 0.140 W (PMC10154928) over its flight muscle 7.6 g x 9.13 % = 0.69 g: 202 W per kg muscle (mean 133). Derived from two sourced numbers; the physiology chain may replace it

inertial_power_W_per_kg_body.source: PMC9490335: flapping inertial power about 8 W/kg body, nearly speed-independent (bat model); subtracted from the available power before thrust

conversion_efficiency.source: P. nathusii 7.0-10.4 % (PMC10154928); used only to report the metabolic and O2 demand, not in the mechanics

validation_targets.source: makiguchi-2013 introduction citing Edgerton and Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990
park-choi-2010 introduction citing Hertel 1966, Rayner 1986, Vogel 1994

validation_targets.quantity: minimum lift-supported speed (constraint C9 in the Lean ledger)
validation_targets.source: physics/results.json interpretation_B from the measured W, S, CL_max

validation_targets.value: at most h_max x (L/D)max = 8 m x 4.37 = 35 m
validation_targets.source: Lean thread's audit 2026-10-31: a pure glide from height h with glide ratio (L/D)max cannot exceed h (L/D)max; long field flights (50 to 400 m) therefore need repeated taxis, ground effect or wind
